links.targetTitle: Revision History panel styling requires scoped CSS on document-editor-context since no props are exposed

title: Revision-history panel visibility is controlled by useRevisionHistoryVisible, showRevisionHistory and hideRevisionHistory
content:
The revision-history panel is rendered by Connect, outside the editor's component tree — which is why it can only be *styled* through scoped CSS. Its *visibility*, though, is ordinary global state with a three-function API:

```ts
function useRevisionHistoryVisible(): boolean | undefined;
function showRevisionHistory(): void;
function hideRevisionHistory(): void;
```

`showRevisionHistory` and `hideRevisionHistory` are plain functions rather than hooks, so they are safe to call from a click handler, an effect, or a keyboard shortcut. Neither takes arguments: the panel always targets the currently selected document, so there is no way to open history for some other document from here.

`useRevisionHistoryVisible` returns `boolean | undefined`, and the third state is meaningful — `undefined` is "not yet initialised" rather than "hidden". Treat it as falsy for rendering, but do not write `visible === false` as your hidden check.

This matters because the toolbar `history` button is not the only sensible affordance. An editor that wants a "see what changed" link inside its own layout, a drive app that opens history on a keyboard shortcut, or an editor that wants to close the panel when the user starts editing again, can all drive the panel directly. The reverse read is equally useful: an editor can consult `useRevisionHistoryVisible()` to collapse a sidebar or suppress its own controls while history is on screen, since the panel takes over the view.

Combined with `disabledControls={["history"]}` on `DocumentToolbar`, these hooks let you remove the built-in button entirely and replace it with your own trigger without losing the feature.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/04-Reference/05-EditorsUI/01-ReactHooks.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
description: Editors can open and close Connect's revision-history panel programmatically instead of relying on the toolbar history button.
